Allergies:
atenolol / Sulfa (Sulfonamide Antibiotics) / trimethoprim / 
Zestril / Penicillins

Chief Complaint:
"I'm okay... more or less."

History of Present Illness:
Briefly, this is a ___ year old woman, history of BPAD type I 
disorder, s/p two prior psychiatric hospitalizations with recent 
discharge from ___ in ___ following an admission 
for mania, no history of suicide attempts, medical history 
significant for hypertension, who presented to ___ ED with her
family due to concerns for worsening depression and inability to 
care for self. 
. 
Upon initial interview, patient reported she was doing well 
following her discharge from ___ 4 in ___ and had returned 
to work, stating she had been functioning at her baseline. 
Approximately one month ago, patient reported she had difficulty 
concentrating at work, difficulty with organization, stating, "I
forgot how to do my job." Over the past few weeks, she reported 
having worsening feelings of hopelessness and worthlessness. She 
presented to the ED 2 weeks ago at ___ due to concerns for 
worsening anxiety and depression and was referred to a PHP at 
___. However, Ms. ___ only attended 4 days of the 
program because she did not like it. 
. 
Over the past two weeks, patient has not been attending work, 
stating all she wants to do is sleep.
. 
Collateral from her cousin, ___ was concerning, 
with her cousin reporting that the patient's condition has  
"gone from bad to worse." The family are concerned for Ms. 
___ ability to care for herself, noting the patient appears 
"paralyzed" and is not washing her clothes, not leaving the
house, or cooking. Patient has also not been attending work and 
has not been in communication with her employer about her 
prolonged absences and she has not been paying her ___. 
Although she has not made explicit suicidal statements, she has 
made vague statements such as, "I don't think I'm going to reach 
the
morning." 
. 
ED Course: patient was in good behavioral control and did not 
require physical or chemical restraints. 
.
On my interview with Ms. ___, who was quite slowed and a 
somewhat unreliable historian, she stated she came to the 
hospital "because I've been anxious and nervous." Reported she 
works as a ___ at a ___ in ___ and is 
"afraid I'm not doing a good job... I want to get ready for work 
but I just can't do it." She went on to report hat "everything 
is stressful-- sometimes I can't remember things that I knew 
from the past and I've been getting evaluations on all the 
things I didn't do." She stated that she had started at a new 
school in ___ and that prior to this she had been in a 
school in ___. She reported the adjustment has been 
difficult, and "I'm asked to do things that teachers usually 
do." Ms. ___ reported that she currently lives with her 
father, who recently had eye surgery and states that things are 
"good." Admitted that she has not been paying her bills, washing 
her clothes, or caring for herself, but was insistent on being 
discharged today or as soon as possible because she feels better 
at home. Stated, "coming here was the worst decision I have ever 
made and now I feel stuck." I assured the patient I would 
discharge her as soon as it was safe to do so. 
. 
Patient reported she has been trying to sleep at home in order 
to "forget the day," but then reported she was only sleeping 4 
hours a night at home. Reported feelings of worthlessness and 
guilt that she is not "able to keep up with my 
responsibilities." Reported poor energy and concentration as 
noted above, reported "okay" appetite, but endorsed a 7 pound 
intentional weight loss since her discharge from ___ in 
___. Denied suicidal ideation or thoughts of self harm, 
denied homicidal ideation. Denied AVH, paranoia. Denied alcohol 
or drug abuse. 
.

Brief Hospital Course:
This is a ___ year old woman, history of BPAD type I disorder, 
s/p two prior psychiatric hospitalizations with recent discharge 
from ___ in ___ following an admission for 
mania, no history of suicide attempts, medical history 
significant for hypertension, who presented to ___ ED with her 
family due to concerns for worsening depression and inability to 
care for self. 
. 
History significant for recent admission to ___ in 
___ for mania with psychotic features characterized by labile 
mood, disorganized thought process, loosening of associations, 
concerns for impulsivity, rapid speech in the setting of ECT 
treatment; patient is now returning to the ED with family with 
apparently
one month of worsening depressive symptoms with low mood, 
disruptions in sleep with significant anxiety and ruminative 
thought process as well as complete inability to care for 
herself as noted in the HPI. Mental status examination is 
notable for disheveled woman with marginal hygiene and grooming 
with slowed speech, decrease prosody, depressed mood, 
significantly blunted affect that is consistent with a 
depressive episode. 
. 
Diagnostically, history and presentation is consistent with BPAD 
with most recent episode depressed, without psychotic features 
at this time. Differential diagnosis also includes underlying 
neurocognitive process, although this seems less likely, and 
which I cannot diagnose at this time in the setting of an acute 
depressive episode, as well as mood disorder secondary to an 
underlying medical condition (unlikely given relatively 
unremarkable medical history and unremarkable laboratory 
examination). Given lack of history of substance use and 
negative tox screen, substance abuse is not a likely contributor 
to her current presentation. 
. 
#. Legal/Safety: Patient was admitted to ___ on a 
___, upon admission, she declined to sign a CV form and a 
petition for a 7&8b hearing was scheduled. However, patient 
later did agree to sign a section 10&11, which was accepted. CV 
signed on ___, 3 day notice signed on ___ were 
filed, patient retracted 3-day notice on ___. Of note, the 
patient did maintain her safety throughout her psychiatric 
hospitalization and did not require physical or chemical 
restraints, although during her initial course she required 
significant redirection and staff support for some dysregulated 
behavior and on one occasion she did take a swing at a staff 
member, which again, did not require physical or chemical 
restraints. 
. 
#. BPAD: type I, most recent episode mixed with psychotic 
features
- Patient with severe depression with poor ADL's, perseverative 
and concrete thought process, significantly depressed mood with 
associated anxiety
- Given bipolar depression, we discussed the risks and benefits 
of initiating Latuda, and the patient was in agreement. 
Risperidone was discontinued and Latuda was started and titrated 
to 80 mg po bid, which she initially tolerated well with no 
complaints of side effects but with limited efficacy. For this 
reason, Zyprexa was started and ultimately titrated to 10 mg po 
qhs and 5 mg po tid prn anxiety and agitation with significant 
improvement in anxiety, agitation, mood lability. Patient was 
also started on Ativan 1 mg po bid prn anxiety. Given 
significant anxiety/agitation and some concern for a mixed 
state, we discussed the risks and benefits of Lithium, which Ms. 
___ initially declined, but she was amenable to starting 
Depakote. Depakote was started at 500 mg po bid which she seemed 
to tolerate well but with ongoing depression and anxiety, 
periods of affective instability. After further discussion of 
the risks and benefits, lithium was initiated and titrated to 
300 mg po qd and 600 mg po qhs. On ___, patient's Depakote 
level was 106 with some concerns for unstable gait, and lithium= 
1.1. Depakote was held given supratherpaeutic level and given 
initiation of ECT (see below) and lithium was decreased to 300 
mg po bid. Patients Depakote was later resumed on ___ at 
250 mg BID and later transitioned to Depakote 500 mg QHS on 
___. On ___ patient was started on Prozac 20 mg daily. 
This was slowly up titrated up to Prozac 60 mg on ___. Due 
to concern for excessive day time sedation Depakote was down 
titrated and discontinued on ___ to avoid polypharmacy and 
sedation. She tolerated this discontinuation well without 
complication.
- Of note, patient was also noted to develop episodes of urinary 
incontinence with unremarkable urinalysis and laboratory 
examination. On ___ patient was also noted to have signs and 
symptoms concerning for catatonia with episodes of staring, 
stiffness, waxy flexibility, automatic obedience. Laboratory 
examination was unremarkable-- no white count, no elevated CK 
and no evidence of autonomic instability. Patient's Latuda was 
held and Ativan was started and titrated to 2 mg po q8h for 
catatonic symptoms with improvement in rigidity, staring spells 
and waxy flexibility. Latuda was subsequently transitioned to 
olanzapine 5 mg po bid. This was later compartmentalized to 
olanzapine 10 mg QHS due to concerns of periods of 
disorientation during evenings, and to target symptoms of 
agitation. The Ativan was slowly down titrated and discontinued 
on ___ due to resolutions of catatonia symptoms while 
receiving ECT (see below) 
- Given the severity of her illness and difficulty treating with 
psychopharmacological agents, I discussed the risks and benefits 
with Ms. ___ and ___ brother, ___ expressed some 
concern for cognitive side effects with the ECT, but both the 
patient and her family agreed to a trial of ECT. 
- Following medical clearance and consultation from Dr. ___ 
___, our ECT specialist, the patient started ECT on 
___ and completed 18 treatments (last as inpatient on ___. 
- By the time of discharge, her presentation had improved 
greatly, with a broader range of affect, improved mood, and 
patient having more energy and able to complete own ADLs. She 
was future oriented and denied SI/HI at the time of discharge. 
She was referred to ___ and D___ services prior to discharge and 
her family was supportive and in agreement with plan. 
- The patient and her family declined referrals to ___ respite 
or to partial program after discharge, expressing strong 
preference for her to return home with her father and cousin, 
who would support her during her recovery. 
.
#. HTN: stable during this admission 
- Continued home Losartan 100 mg po qd 

#. GERD: stable 
- Continued home Pantoprazole 40 mg po bid 
.
#. D___
- D___ services were applied for and a needs and means assessment 
was completed. ___ will continue to follow patient after 
discharge. ___ Contact - ___ - ___
.
#. OT - OTAPS assessment
-The patient completed an OTAPS assessment with Occupational 
Therapy on ___. 
Overall assessment: Based on assessment results, patient 
interview, team report and
OMR, it is strongly recommended that she receives additional
assistance at home upon discharge. She would benefit from ___ 
services to ensure safe medication adherence.  ___ visiting RN 
could also monitor patient's mental status and identify 
potential safety hazards in her home environment.  Patient would 
also
benefit from support around managing her finances. 
-Patient was referred to ___ services prior to discharge and her 
brother and family were assisting her in managing her finances.

Discharge Diagnosis:
BPAD, type I, most recent episode depressed with catatonic 
features
